_note: The proposals that are not about the deficit: two that move money in opposite directions, one that binds a spending line, and the one that makes the bloc act as a single power against the nations outside it. See docs/bloc-model.md. V4.5b sponsors and decision classes, placed by tools/council_probe.gd table T. cohesion_fund and recovery_facility are UNANIMITY: multiannual-budget and own-resources matters are, and the real recovery fund rode the Own Resources Decision through unanimity and national ratification. common_external_tariff stays qualified majority, because trade policy is. Under unanimity cohesion_fund's 0.28 call drew 26 vetoes at every cell of the sweep grid. The transfer term prices every member as a payer, and nobody draws on the fund, so no position could carry it. Under qualified majority it had never opened in a 168-month run either. It now calls 0.05, at (-0.4, 0.0), and its sponsor is PRT, the friends-of-cohesion member. POL, the first choice, vetoed its own proposal: the sponsor is the one member that never lobbies itself. The one veto left is CZE.

proposals.name: Cohesion Fund Expansion
proposals.summary: A larger common fund for the bloc's poorer regions, paid for by a higher call on every member's budget.

proposals.name: Recovery and Resilience Facility
proposals.summary: Joint borrowing against the bloc's own credit, disbursed to members as investment grants. Cheaper than borrowing alone, and it is the bloc's balance sheet that carries it.

proposals.name: Common External Tariff
proposals.summary: The bloc levies as one on goods entering from outside it. Every member's customs post charges the same rate, and no member sets its own.
